newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Telekom to get $45.2 mln development loan.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Telekom to get $45.2 mln development loan.

text.p: Slovenian state-owned telecommunications company Telekom said on Tuesday it would receive a 6.4 billion tolars ($45.2 million) development loan from a group of six foreign banks next year.
The banks are Austria's Creditanstalt-Bankverein, Germany's Dresdner Bank AG and Bank Gesellschaft Berlin AG, Bank Luxembourg, ING Barings, Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank and Credit Suisse.

Telekom spokesman Boris Ziherl said the company would use the loan, the biggest granted to a Slovenian state-owned firm without a state guarantee, to develop and modernise the telecommunications network over the next two years.
Telekom will repay the money over 85 months under the condition that it starts repayments two years after it receives the loan. The interest rate is 0.35 percent over LIBOR.
"This amount of money will cover a third of our annual investments. This year we expect investments to reach 20 billion tolars," Ziherl said.
In 1996 Telekom made 50,000 new telephone connections and planned the same pace of expansion over the next three years, he continued.
He forecast that by the end of 1998 Slovenia would have 40 telephones per 100 inhabitants, compared with 33 telephones at present and an average 46 telephones in the European Union.
"Slovenia is already at the level of some less developed EU countries like Spain, Portugal and Greece," Ziherl said.
Telekom, which should complete its privatisation by the middle of next year, is expected to keep control of about 74 percent of shares.
